text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Head of General Staff Ismail Karadayi draws attention to recent incidents in Afghanistan, where hardline Islamist militia is now in control, and hints they may pose a risk for Turkey.
- Deputies from two conservative parties, coalition member True Path Party and main opposition Motherland, working out new formula for a union of right-wing forces.
- Scandal in the opening of the university term as Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan shows interest in an Arab lecturer who insulted the national anthem in ceremonies held in Konya.
- Leftist party has prepared its report on the southeast.
- A draft law giving wives the authority to make claims of spousal rape is being prepared by the Motherland Party.
- Appeals court issues decision on October 3 in case of 124 Islamist militants charged in connection with hotel fire that killed dozens of secularist intellectuals.

- Turkey fails to collect its debts and wastes time on new economic packages. Islamist-led government has already unveiled two packages aiming to raise state revenues and another is said to be on the way.
- Conservative coalition partner joins an opposition protest against Islamist premier's visit to Libya.
- European environmentalists will come to Turkey to study projects of a foundation fighting erosion.
